title: DOJ Launches Fresh Attempt to Prosecute Former FBI Director James Comey
snippet: Federal prosecutors are seeking to charge former FBI Director James Comey over an alleged decade-old classified leak, marking the Trump administration's third effort to bring criminal charges against the vocal critic.
content:
WASHINGTON — In the latest escalation of a high-profile feud, federal prosecutors are once again pursuing criminal charges against former FBI Director James Comey, according to unsealed federal court documents in Washington, D.C.

The Justice Department is targeting Comey over an alleged leak of classified information dating back ten years. Comey's legal team immediately pushed back, arguing the effort is legally flawed and far past the standard statute of limitations for federal prosecution.

Comey Decries 'Appalling Abuse'

The newly revealed court records expose a fierce dispute that has unfolded behind closed doors over the past month. The filing represents the third attempt by prosecutors to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime adversary of President Donald Trump, since Trump returned to the White House.

Comey forcefully rejected the accusations in a video statement shortly after the documents dropped. "Well, they’re back — again," Comey said. "It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice – one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing’s changed with me; I’m still innocent, I’m still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in an independent federal judiciary."

Legal Maneuvers Around Time Limits

To bypass the 10-year legal window for bringing charges, the Justice Department filed a formal legal document known as a criminal information, aiming to freeze—or "toll"—the clock on the statute of limitations.

A Justice Department spokesperson defended the procedure, stating, "Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further."

A Fractured History

Comey led the FBI under former President Barack Obama after serving as a senior Justice Department official during the George W. Bush administration. His relationship with Trump collapsed shortly after the 2016 election, sparked in part by Comey's refusal to pledge personal loyalty to the president during a private dinner—an interaction Comey documented in a detailed memo at the time.

Trump fired Comey in May 2017 while the FBI was investigating potential ties between Russia and the Trump campaign. That probe was later handed over to Special Counsel Robert Mueller, whose final report documented Russian election interference and welcoming signals from the Trump campaign, but stopped short of establishing a criminal conspiracy.
